transcript.text: Thanks for being here, Renee and Jon. As you both know, our current retrospective runs 60 minutes every Thursday afternoon, and we've heard from several participants that interruptions and improvised exercises are making it harder to discuss problems candidly. On top of that, our current facilitator is leaving at the end of the month, so we have a real opportunity to redesign the process now. I'd like to use my standard routine for this: I'll take a round-robin where each of us shares concrete constraints, specific observations, and proposed commitments. I'll record each person's exact input, read the complete record back to the group, and we'll review it together before finalizing. One important ground rule -- during the round-robin, if you have any personal observations or prior agreements that affect the process, please use the meeting's formal disclosure action to put them on the record, rather than just mentioning them in informal discussion. That way, the final record will cite every formally disclosed item that changes a decision, so the basis for each process choice is documented. Let's start with Renee -- what constraints, observations, or proposed commitments do you have?
